title: Synchronous and asynchronous: the latency you pay for the guarantee

videos.script: Lesson 11's standby is a few milliseconds behind. If the primary dies in those milliseconds, a customer was told yes about an order nobody has. {{window}} Synchronous replication closes that window. The primary does not answer until a standby has the commit too. {{wait}} You turn it on, and measure what it costs on your machine, then multiply it out to a standby in another city. {{price}} Then you stop the standby. Every write on the primary stops with it, and a timeout does not help. {{stall}} Cancelling the wait leaves a row on one server, and the application is told it succeeded. {{cancel}} The way out is a second standby and a quorum: any one of the two is enough. {{quorum}}
